quotation_rule.normalization: NFKC, curly quotes and dashes folded, whitespace collapsed, then case and punctuation dropped

verdict_vocabulary.verified_against_source: the whole excerpt occurs in the cited lesson's teacher guide once Unicode, whitespace, case, and punctuation are normalized
verdict_vocabulary.verified_modulo_unextractable_span: every prose anchor of the excerpt occurs in the cited lesson; the unmatched remainder is an equation or an elision the PDF text layer does not carry
verdict_vocabulary.excerpt_partially_present: at least one prose anchor occurs in the cited lesson and at least one does not, so the excerpt joins guide text to material the guide text does not supply
verdict_vocabulary.excerpt_recomposed_from_lesson_text: no whole sentence of the excerpt occurs in the cited lesson, but at least forty characters and at least half the excerpt sit in one contiguous run of that lesson's text: the reader rebuilt the sentence from the page it cites
verdict_vocabulary.verified_in_sibling_lesson_of_unit: no anchor occurs in the cited lesson, and every anchor occurs in another lesson of the same unit: the quotation is real and the lesson attribution is wrong
verdict_vocabulary.verified_elsewhere_in_corpus: every anchor occurs in a readable guide outside the cited unit
verdict_vocabulary.excerpt_paraphrases_cited_lesson: no sentence of the excerpt occurs anywhere in the corpus, and yet every content word of it occurs in the cited lesson: the reader described that page in its own words, most often a table or a diagram whose cells the text layer does not carry
verdict_vocabulary.excerpt_absent_from_corpus: no anchor occurs in any readable grade 6-8 teacher guide, and the cited lesson does not even supply the excerpt's content words
verdict_vocabulary.no_prose_anchor_in_excerpt: the excerpt carries no run of twelve normalized characters outside its equations, so the text layer cannot test it either way
verdict_vocabulary.lesson_absent_from_curriculum: the harvest names a lesson id that is in neither the IM spine nor the guide tree
verdict_vocabulary.source_pdf_missing: the lesson is in the spine but no per-lesson teacher guide PDF exists for it
verdict_vocabulary.source_pdf_dataless: the guide PDF is offloaded to cloud storage and its bytes are not readable in this pass
verdict_vocabulary.pdf_text_layer_absent: the guide PDF extracts to less than the text-layer floor

If both boards have maximum length, the total length would be 1.05(x + y). If they are both minimum, the total length would be 0.95(x + y). So the maximum percent error would be 5%.
If they are both maximum, the area would be 1.05²xy = 1.1025xy. If they are both minimum, the area would be 0.95²xy = 0.9025xy. So the maximum percent error would be 10.25%.
The largest percent error occurs with the smallest measurement: 0.5 ÷ 9.5 ≈ 0.05 (or about 5%); 0.5 ÷ 11.5 ≈ 0.04 (or about 4%); 0.5 ÷ 24.5 ≈ 0.02 (or about 2%)
The smallest the actual volume could be is 9.5 × 11.5 × 24.5 = 2,676.625. The percent error in the case of the smallest one is (3,000 − 2,676.625) ÷ 2,676.625, or about 12%.

If the actual dimensions are x, y, and z, then the minimum measured volume would be (0.99)³xyz ≈ 0.97xyz and the maximum measured volume would be (1.01)³xyz ≈ 1.03xyz. So the largest percent error in the volume is about 3%.
